# The workspace: cycles, teams, names, leaving and what needs attention

What Workspace says about each cycle and team, the longest name a workspace may have, who may leave, and what its overview lists as needing attention.

## The rule

**A cycle** (a goal year) says how many goals it has and how many check-ins were posted on them (removed ones don't count), and so whether it can be deleted: only when nobody has checked in to it **and** it isn't the only cycle. The only cycle always stays, so a new workspace's cycle says so rather than offering Delete. Each cycle shows its first and last days (its start date, then `weeks × 7 − 1` days on) and whether it is running (with its week), not started yet, or over.

**A team's people** are everyone in it, and its lead even when the lead's own team is another; the lead counts once.

**A workspace's name** is 3 to 80 characters, after trimming and joining spaces. Nothing cuts it short: the field counts the characters once a name is within 20 of the limit, and a longer name is refused with how long it is.

**Leaving.** Anyone may leave a workspace themselves. It is the same as an admin marking them as left (whoever takes over their goals and open asks is chosen first; they leave the reviews they were in), logged as "Name left the workspace". The only admin may not leave.

**What needs attention** on the overview, most pressing first: the year ending (the wrap-up open, or opening within 4 weeks); no goals in the cycle; then, for admins only, fewer than 3 people, people with no email, people in no team, teams with no lead, and no review set up; then new markups and feedback sent from this workspace. Admins are told what only they can fix; everyone is told what anyone can.

## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| A new workspace: one cycle, no goals, no check-ins. | `No goals and no check-ins yet; it’s the only cycle, so it stays` |
| The same workspace with a second cycle nobody has checked in to. | `No goals and no check-ins yet: it can be deleted` |
| One goal with two check-ins, in the only cycle. | `1 goal, 2 check-ins: it stays` |
| A team led by Lee, who is in it, with Pat in it too. | `2 people` |
| A workspace name of 83 characters. | `Keep the name to 80 characters or fewer: it has 83.` |
| A workspace name of 62 characters, as it is typed. | `62 of 80 characters` |
| Lee, the only admin, leaves. | `refused: You’re the only admin here: make someone else an admin before you leave.` |
| What needs attention for an admin in week 2: two people with no email, one goal, no review, 4 new markups from here. | `few-people, no-email, no-review, feedback` |
| The same, for Pat, who isn’t an admin. | `feedback` |

## Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** How many weeks before the wrap-up "ends soon" starts (four) is a choice, not a law; the rebuild may tune it.
- **Not self-explanatory:** Leaving with no goals and no history still marks the person as left (they can be restored), unlike an admin deleting someone with no history.

## Requirements

- `WORKSPACE-ONE-PLACE`: Workspace is one place (backlog WS). The sidebar's header (and a phone's top bar) is the workspace switcher: it names the open workspace, lists every workspace, says whether you're an admin here, and offers setting up a workspace of your own (not Home). Switching is navigation with a history entry, so Back returns to the workspace you came from; you land on the same kind of page or Home, never on the old workspace's goal; while the other loads the screen says "Opening <name>…"; part-way through a task with a draft it asks first and says the draft stays in its own workspace. The person menu is only about people. Your role shows: "Admin" beside your name where you are one, and Workspace says your permissions in one line (what is for admins, and who they are). The overview lists what needs attention here first (domain/workspaceAttention), then every section. Cycles show their dates, which is running, their goals and check-ins, and their actions; a team counts its lead and opens its people; a workspace name's 80-character limit is said while typing, never cut; no button clips its label.
